title: Derived restriction of scalars from finite to completed integral coefficients
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell\neq p$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, a scheme $Y$, and put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$. Let $\pi_n:\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}\twoheadrightarrow(A_{E,n})_Y$ be the projection of the completed coefficient sheaf on $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and $\operatorname{Res}_n:\Sh(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})\to\Sh(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ the restriction of scalars along $\pi_n$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], an exact functor [lem-weil-restriction-of-scalars-exact]. Let $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})$ and $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ be the derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of $\Sh(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})$ and of $\Sh(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$. Applying $\operatorname{Res}_n$ termwise to complexes sends quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms (an exact functor commutes with cohomology objects), and so defines the functor

$$
 \operatorname{Res}_n:D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})\longrightarrow D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E),\qquad \operatorname{Res}_n(Q(M))=Q(\operatorname{Res}_n M)
$$

on complexes $M$ of $(A_{E,n})_Y$-modules, and on morphisms by the universal property of the localization $Q$; it commutes with the shift. It is the *derived restriction of scalars*.

source.place: Stacks Project, Derived Categories, Lemma 'right-derived-exact-functor' (Tag 015F): an exact functor of abelian categories transforms quasi-isomorphisms into quasi-isomorphisms, and every complex computes its derived functor on D; used in Bhatt-Scholze (literature/bhatt-scholze-pro-etale-topology_arXiv-1309.1198.pdf) p. 24, Proposition 3.5.1 and Definition 3.5.2, where the reductions K⊗^L R/m^n are read in D(X, R^) through the algebra maps R^ → R/m^n
